name: prop
description: A small object that fills a scene.
conventions: A prop's origin is at the centre of its base on the ground; objects that sit on others (a cup on a table) are modelled sitting at y = 0 too.
anticipate: A single simple collision box; props are placed in numbers.

name: crate
description: A crate or box.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard

name: barrel
description: A barrel, drum or tank.

scale.source: a standard 55 gallon (208 L) steel drum is about 0.57 m across and 0.88 m high

pitfalls: Make the profile with a lathe: a plain cylinder misses the rolling hoops and the chime at the rim.

name: shipping container
description: An ISO intermodal container.

parts.name: Door
parts.note: Double doors at the rear (-Z), hinged at the outer edges, with locking rods.

scale.source: ISO 668: width 8 ft = 2.438 m, standard height 8 ft 6 in = 2.591 m (high cube 9 ft 6 in = 2.896 m), length 20 ft = 6.058 m or 40 ft = 12.192 m

pitfalls: The wall is corrugated: a flat box loses the look; use a normal map or real corrugations.

name: chair
description: A chair, stool or seat.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard; seat height about 0.42-0.48 m

name: table
description: A table or desk.

scale.source: table and desk height is typically 0.72-0.76 m (general knowledge)

name: campfire
description: A fire for cooking and warmth: logs in a pile or a tripod, usually a ring of stones, and a flame.

parts.name: Logs
parts.note: Laid crossed or leaning in a cone; each log a cylinder with a slightly rough end.

parts.name: Stones
parts.note: A ring of rocks around the fire; they sit on the ground.

parts.name: Flame
parts.note: An emissive shape or a marker for a fire effect: a flame is not solid geometry.

parts.name: Embers
parts.note: A glowing bed under the logs.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical range, not a standard

anticipate: Fire is an effect, not a mesh: model the logs and stones, and put an empty node at the flame origin for the particles and a PointLight.
The flame's glow as an emissive material, so it shows in the dark without a light.
Logs and stones as separate nodes, so the fire can burn down by hiding logs.
pitfalls: A fire modelled as a solid orange cone looks like a traffic cone; leave the flame to particles.
Logs sunk into the ground or floating above it: they rest on the ground or on each other.

name: door
description: A hinged door in its frame, as in a house or a building.

parts.name: Leaf
parts.note: The pivot sits on the hinge line at one vertical edge, not in the middle of the leaf.

scale.source: general knowledge: common interior and front door leaves are about 0.73-0.93 m wide and 2.0-2.1 m high (in the Netherlands 0.83 x 2.015 m is a common size, in the US 32 x 80 in = 0.81 x 2.03 m); not a single standard

pitfalls: A door that swings around its centre: put the Leaf's origin on the hinge edge.
The handle belongs on the edge away from the hinges, at about 1.0-1.05 m above the floor.

name: ladder
description: A leaning ladder with two rails and rungs.

parts.name: Rung
parts.note: Rungs are about 0.25-0.30 m apart.

scale.source: general knowledge: single leaning ladders are about 0.4-0.5 m wide with rungs about 0.28 m apart (EN 131 sets the rules for portable ladders); length varies with use

pitfalls: Rungs pushed into the rails leave hidden faces; end them at the inner side of each rail.
For climbing, add a collision shape and a climb area separate from the visual mesh.

name: tent
description: A camping tent: a dome or ridge tent on the ground.

scale.source: general knowledge: two- to four-person dome tents are about 2-3 m long and 1.0-1.5 m high; family tents are larger

pitfalls: The canvas is single-sided cloth: make it double-sided or give it thickness, or it disappears from inside.
Stand it on y = 0 with the pegs into the ground, not floating above it.

name: well
description: A water well: a round wall over a shaft, often with a roof and a winch.

parts.name: Shaft
parts.note: A dark disc a little below the rim is cheaper than a deep shaft.

scale.source: general knowledge: the wall of a traditional well is about 1-1.5 m across and 0.7-1 m high; with a roof it reaches about 2.5 m

pitfalls: A wall made from a closed cylinder hides the opening; build it as a ring (a tube or a lathe profile).
The winch turns about its own axle: put its pivot on the axle between the two posts.

name: bed
description: A bed with a frame and mattress, for one or two sleepers.

scale.source: General knowledge of typical household furniture dimensions, not a standard or manufacturer specification. A single mattress is commonly about 0.9 x 2.0 m.

pitfalls: Keep the mattress separate from the frame; the frame should support it rather than intersect its visible top.

name: sofa
description: A sofa or couch with a shared frame and space for multiple people.

scale.source: General knowledge of typical household furniture dimensions, not a standard or manufacturer specification. Width spans compact two-seat and larger sofas.

pitfalls: A sofa is a shared seating unit, not a single chair stretched without changing the frame and cushions.

name: bookcase
description: A freestanding bookcase or bookshelf with stacked shelves.

scale.source: General knowledge of typical household furniture dimensions, not a standard or manufacturer specification. Freestanding domestic shelving is usually shallower than a wardrobe.

pitfalls: Leave usable space between shelves; solid stacked boxes do not read as open shelving.

name: cupboard
description: A storage cupboard, cabinet or wardrobe with hinged doors and shelves.

scale.source: General knowledge of typical household furniture dimensions, not a standard or manufacturer specification. Wardrobes are commonly deeper than kitchen wall cupboards.

pitfalls: Put each door pivot at its vertical hinge edge, not at the centre of the leaf.

name: bench
description: A park or street bench with a long shared seat.

scale.source: General knowledge of park furniture: shared seats are commonly about 1.5-2.0 m wide with seats around 0.45 m high; not a standard.

pitfalls: Keep the long shared seat distinct from the optional back; do not inherit a single-chair silhouette.

name: bin
description: A street waste bin or trash can, with an opening and optional lid.

scale.source: General knowledge of small public waste bins and household trash cans; dimensions vary by capacity, not a standard.

pitfalls: Keep an actual opening or dark recess visible instead of sealing the top with a solid cap.

name: mailbox
description: A letter box or mailbox with a mail slot and an access door.

scale.source: General knowledge of residential letter boxes, wall-mounted or on a post; not a postal regulation.

pitfalls: A wall-mounted box needs a flat mounting face; a freestanding box needs a supporting post.

name: sword
description: A sword: a long straight blade with a crossguard, a grip and a pommel, from a one-handed arming sword to a two-handed longsword or a fantasy blade.

parts.name: Blade
parts.note: Double edged and tapering to a point, with a fuller down the middle; the flat of the blade faces +Z.

parts.name: Guard
parts.note: Crosses the blade along x at the bottom of the blade.

parts.name: Grip
parts.note: Wrapped in leather or cord; its node is where a hand holds the sword.

scale.source: general knowledge of surviving medieval swords (Oakeshott typology): one-handed arming swords are about 0.8-1.0 m long overall, longswords about 1.1-1.3 m, with a crossguard 0.15-0.3 m wide

conventions: A sword stands upright with the end of the pommel on y = 0 and the point up (+Y); the guard runs along x and the flat of the blade faces +Z.
Attach it to a hand at the Grip node; the blade's point is at the top of the bounding box.
anticipate: A thin box or capsule collider along the blade for hits, separate from the grip.
pitfalls: A blade as a flat box has no edge: give it a diamond or lenticular section that thins to the edges and to the point.
A sword is long and thin: about 0.8-1.3 m, with a blade only 4-6 cm wide at the guard.

name: shield
description: A hand-held shield: a round, heater or kite shaped board with a rim, a boss in the middle and a grip on the back.

parts.name: Board
parts.note: Slightly domed or curved planks, faced with leather or paint; the front faces +Z.

parts.name: Grip
parts.note: On the back (-Z), behind the boss on a round shield.

scale.source: general knowledge of museum finds and reconstructions: the Gokstad ship burial round shields are about 0.94 m across, bucklers 0.3-0.45 m, heater shields about 0.6-0.9 m high, kite shields up to about 1.2 m

conventions: A shield stands upright on its lowest point at y = 0 with its face towards +Z; the grip is on the back (-Z).
Attach it to the forearm or the hand at the Grip node.
pitfalls: A shield is not flat: a round shield's board is slightly domed and a heater shield is curved around the body.
The boss is a hollow dome over a hole in the board, with the hand grip right behind it.

name: battle axe
description: A battle axe: an iron head with one or two crescent blades on a long wooden haft.

parts.name: Haft
parts.note: Wood, slightly oval in section, with a leather grip wrap near the end.

parts.name: Head
parts.note: The eye of the head wraps around the haft near its top.

parts.name: Blade
parts.note: Crescent shaped and thin at the edge; a double axe has one on each side (along x).

scale.source: general knowledge of Viking-age finds and reconstructions: one-handed axes have a haft of about 0.6-0.9 m, a two-handed Dane axe about 1.2-1.7 m, with a cutting edge of about 0.1-0.3 m

conventions: The axe stands upright with the end of the haft on y = 0 and the head at the top; the blade points along +X (and -X for a double axe), its flat faces +Z.
pitfalls: The head is thin at the edge and thick at the eye: a flat box reads as a sign, not a blade.

name: potion bottle
description: A small glass bottle or flask with a coloured liquid and a cork, as a game pickup or on an apothecary's shelf.

parts.name: Bottle
parts.note: Transparent glass with a visible thickness; the lip at the top is a little thicker.

parts.name: Liquid
parts.note: A separate mesh inside the glass up to the fill level, with a flat top; it may glow (emissive).

scale.source: laboratory glassware: ISO 1773 Erlenmeyer flasks of 100-250 ml are about 64-85 mm across and 105-145 mm tall; small apothecary bottles and vials are 50-150 mm tall

conventions: The bottle stands on y = 0; the liquid is its own node inside the glass so its colour and fill level can change.
anticipate: The liquid is drawn after the glass: give the glass alphaMode BLEND and the liquid an opaque material so sorting stays stable.
pitfalls: Liquid exactly on the glass surface z-fights: keep it a wall thickness inside.
Opaque glass hides the liquid; the glass needs BLEND with a low alpha.

name: treasure chest
description: A wooden treasure chest with a barrel-vaulted lid on hinges, iron bands and corners, a lock plate at the front and handles at the ends.

parts.name: Lid
parts.note: Hinged at the back top edge (-Z) about x; opening turns the front up and back.

parts.name: Band
parts.note: Iron straps over the planks and corner fittings.

scale.source: general knowledge of wooden chests and travel trunks: about 0.6-1.0 m long, 0.4-0.6 m deep and 0.4-0.7 m high with the lid closed

conventions: The front with the lock faces +Z; the lid's pivot is on its back hinge line, so lid.rotation.x = -angle opens it.
pitfalls: A lid that turns about its middle: put the Lid origin on the back hinge line.
Iron bands floating off the wood: they lie on the planks with a few millimetres of thickness.

name: oil lantern
description: A hanging oil lantern: a fuel tank at the bottom, a glass globe around a burning wick, a wire guard or frame, a vented cap and a bail handle to hang it by.

parts.name: Glass
parts.note: Clear glass (BLEND) around the flame.

parts.name: Frame
parts.note: Wire guards or corner posts that protect the glass and carry the cap.

parts.name: Handle
parts.note: A bail that swings about x at the two points where it meets the lantern; its origin is on that line.

parts.name: Flame
parts.note: Emissive; a PointLight goes at its node.

scale.source: general knowledge: a common hurricane lantern (such as the Feuerhand 276) is about 0.26 m tall and 0.15 m across without its handle; carriage and ship lanterns reach about 0.5 m

conventions: The lantern stands on its base at y = 0 with the handle up; hang it from the handle's top. Put a PointLight at the Flame node.
anticipate: A warm PointLight with a short distance at the flame; the emissive flame alone does not light the scene.
pitfalls: Opaque glass hides the flame: give the glass BLEND with a low alpha.
The flame is tiny (2-4 cm) compared with the lantern.

name: teapot
description: A teapot: a round belly turned on a wheel, a curved spout at the front, a loop handle at the back and a lid with a knob.

parts.name: Body
parts.note: A surface of revolution (lathe) with a foot ring and an opening at the top.

parts.name: Spout
parts.note: Rises from the lower belly at the front (+Z) to above the rim, so the pot can be full.

parts.name: Handle
parts.note: A loop at the back (-Z), wide enough for fingers.

scale.source: general knowledge of household teapots: a 1-1.5 litre pot is about 0.13-0.2 m tall and 0.22-0.3 m from spout to handle

conventions: The teapot stands on its foot at y = 0 with the spout towards +Z and the handle at -Z.
pitfalls: The spout's tip must reach above the rim of the body, or the tea would pour out before the pot is full.
A spout and handle that stop short of the body float: sink their ends a little into the belly.

name: grandfather clock
description: A longcase (grandfather) clock: a tall wooden case on a plinth, a hood with a glazed dial and hands, and a swinging pendulum and weights behind a door in the trunk.

parts.name: Case
parts.note: The tall middle section (the trunk) on a wider plinth.

parts.name: Hood
parts.note: The top section that holds the dial, often with a pediment or crest.

parts.name: Dial
parts.note: Faces +Z behind a glazed door.

parts.name: Hand
parts.note: Each hand turns about z at the centre of the dial; its origin is on that arbor, not in the middle of the hand.

parts.name: Pendulum
parts.note: Swings about z from its suspension at the top; a seconds pendulum is 0.994 m long.

scale.source: general knowledge of longcase clocks: usually 1.9-2.4 m tall, 0.4-0.6 m wide at the hood and 0.25-0.35 m deep; the seconds pendulum that defines them is 0.994 m long

conventions: The clock stands on y = 0 with the dial facing +Z. Animate the hands by rotation.z about their own origin (negative is clockwise seen from the front) and the pendulum by rotation.z = A * sin(pi * t) for a seconds pendulum.
pitfalls: The pendulum pivots at its suspension spring at the top, not at the bob: put its origin there.
A clock hand with its origin in its middle spins like a propeller: put the origin on the dial centre.
